examples.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Integral Containing an Arbitrary Logarithm
examples.worked_solution:
We define

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{4}⁡x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡4} \\ {v}^{′}=\frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x=-\,\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{log}_{4}⁡x}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={log}_{4}⁡x(-\,\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}})-\int (-\,\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}})\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}}\,{log}_{4}⁡x+\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\int \frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{2{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡4}+\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡4}(-\,\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}})+C \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{2{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡4}-\frac{1}{4{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡4}+C \\  & =-\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x+1}{4{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡4}+C,\end{aligned}
$$

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula $\log_4{x}=\dfrac{\ln{x}}{\ln{4}}.$

feedback.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x & \,⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=\frac{1}{{x}^{2}} & \,⟹\,v=\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\,dx=-\frac{1}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{4}}\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{{e}^{4}}u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv{|}_{1}^{{e}^{4}}-{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{4}}v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x(-\frac{1}{x}){|}_{1}^{{e}^{4}}-{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{4}}(-\frac{1}{x})(\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =[\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{4})(-\frac{1}{{e}^{4}})-\operatorname{ln}⁡(1)(-\frac{1}{1})]+{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{4}}\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{4}{{e}^{4}}\operatorname{ln}⁡(e)-\frac{1}{x}{|}_{1}^{{e}^{4}} \\  & =-\frac{4}{{e}^{4}}-(\frac{1}{{e}^{4}}-\frac{1}{1}) \\  & =1-5{e}^{-4}.\end{aligned}
$$
